notes: ACTIVE relation pack (upgraded from pilot). No invented Sn/Sp. Traditional MTrP maps labeled traditional. No Travell verbatim.

relations.source_structure: ankle / midfoot fracture clinical decision rule construct
relations.clinical_context: Acute ankle or midfoot trauma; apply Ottawa Ankle Rules before assuming simple sprain.
supporting_evidence: Ottawa Ankle Rules validated to reduce unnecessary radiographs while catching clinically relevant fractures

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Cite Bachmann 2003 only. High Sn for excluding fracture — not a sprain test. See cited-diagnostic-accuracy.md.

limitations: Not a soft-tissue sprain diagnostic tool
Intoxication, delayed presentation, and some populations need clinical judgment
recommended_examination: If rules negative → functional sprain / syndesmosis screen as indicated

references.citation: Stiell IG et al. Decision rules for the use of radiography in acute ankle injuries (Ottawa Ankle Rules). JAMA / related validation papers.
Bachmann LM et al. Accuracy of Ottawa ankle rules — systematic review / meta-analysis (qualitative: useful high-sensitivity rule).

relations.clinical_context: Inversion mechanism with lateral pain/swelling; anterior drawer negative, especially early after injury.
supporting_evidence: Drawer testing reliability and timing-dependent usefulness are limited in acute phase
Clinical diagnosis of lateral sprain is primarily history + location + Ottawa-negative fracture screen

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp. Negative drawer ≠ ligaments cleared.

limitations: Pain, swelling, and guarding reduce validity acutely
recommended_examination: Talar tilt / squeeze / external rotation for syndesmosis suspicion
Functional load progression rather than single laxity test exclusion

references.citation: Vuurberg G et al. Diagnosis, treatment and prevention of ankle sprains: update of an evidence-based clinical guideline. BJSM.
Croy T et al. Anterior drawer reliability / validity discussions in ankle instability literature (qualitative limitations).

relations.source_structure: lumbar nerve root / S1 pathway clinical
relations.clinical_context: Foot or heel pain without clear local mechanical findings; lumbar or radicular clues present.
supporting_evidence: Radicular and somatic referred pain can present distally
Negative local ankle drawer does not address proximal neural sources

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Pattern-based differential; no numeric referral accuracy.

limitations: Most plantar heel pain is local fascia-related — do not over-call lumbar
Neurological exam required before claiming radicular
recommended_examination: SLR / neurological screen when proximal clues
Windlass / fascia palpation for heel pain
red_flags: Cauda features if accompanied by severe lumbar neurological change

references.citation: Delitto A et al. Low Back Pain CPG — referred and radicular pain framing.
Martin RL et al. Heel Pain — Plantar Fasciitis CPG. JOSPT.

relations.clinical_context: Sudden pop, weakness of push-off; calf squeeze without plantarflexion.
supporting_evidence: Thompson / Simmonds test is a standard clinical screen for complete Achilles rupture

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Useful clinical screen; still confirm per local pathway. Do not invent exact Sn/Sp in this JSON.

recommended_examination: Thompson + gap palpation + Matles if trained
Urgent imaging / ortho pathway when rupture suspected
Do not treat as 'calf strain' if Thompson positive
red_flags: Suspected complete rupture — timely specialist pathway

references.citation: Thompson TC / Simmonds FA classical descriptions; modern Achilles rupture diagnostic reviews.
Garras DN et al. / Achilles rupture clinical diagnosis literature — combination of signs preferred.

relations.source_structure: plantar fascia / plantar heel pain construct
relations.clinical_context: First-step heel pain with possible calf tightness, load-training errors, or lumbar clues.
supporting_evidence: Plantar fasciitis CPGs emphasize load and contributing factors; proximal contributors are hypotheses not automatic causes

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Coexistence framing — not a single-test metric.

limitations: Do not auto-blame 'tight calves' or MTrP as sole cause
Windlass negative does not fully exclude fascia-related pain
recommended_examination: Windlass + fascia palpation with familiar pain
Calcaneal squeeze if stress fracture suspicion
red_flags: Night pain progressive — tumor/infection uncommon but screen history

references.citation: Martin RL et al. Heel Pain — Plantar Fasciitis: Revision CPG. JOSPT.
Riddle DL / plantar heel pain clinical literature — contributing factors framing.

relations.clinical_context: Inversion or ER/DF mechanism with pain above the ATFL; recovery slower than simple lateral sprain.
supporting_evidence: Syndesmosis injury is a key differential from lateral ligament sprain
Squeeze / external-rotation tests are clinical screens with imperfect accuracy

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp for squeeze or ER stress.

recommended_examination: Squeeze / ER stress with familiar pain

references.citation: Vuurberg G et al. Ankle sprain guideline update. BJSM.
Syndesmosis clinical diagnosis reviews — qualitative mixed special-test performance.

relations.source_structure: plantar fascia / plantar heel pain construct
relations.clinical_context: First-step heel pain typical of plantar heel pain; Windlass negative or poorly tolerated.
supporting_evidence: Plantar fasciitis CPGs: clinical pattern + localized tenderness matter; single provocation imperfect

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Negative Windlass ≠ fascia-related pain excluded. No invented Sn/Sp.

recommended_examination: Calcaneal squeeze if stress fracture suspicion

references.citation: Martin RL et al. Heel Pain — Plantar Fasciitis CPG. JOSPT.
Riddle DL / plantar heel pain clinical literature — contributing factors framing.

relations.clinical_context: Lateral ankle pain with eversion/resisted eversion or instability history; may be labelled chronic sprain.
supporting_evidence: Peroneal tendinopathy/subluxation is a recognized lateral ankle differential

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp for peroneal provocation.

recommended_examination: Resisted eversion / tendon palpation with familiar pain

references.citation: Vuurberg G et al. Ankle sprain guideline — differentials framing. BJSM.
Peroneal tendon clinical assessment reviews — qualitative limitations.

relations.clinical_context: Sudden mileage increase, osteoporosis risk, progressive heel pain; calcaneal squeeze reproduces familiar pain.
supporting_evidence: Stress fracture is a key serious differential for plantar heel pain

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Squeeze is a clinical screen — do not invent Sn/Sp; imaging when suspicion high.

limitations: Do not delay imaging if high suspicion
recommended_examination: Do not progress impact load if suspicion high

references.citation: Martin RL et al. Heel Pain CPG — differential including stress fracture. JOSPT.
Stress fracture clinical screening literature — qualitative risk and squeeze framing.

relations.source_structure: midfoot / fifth metatarsal fracture clinical decision construct
relations.clinical_context: Acute midfoot trauma meeting Ottawa midfoot criteria — imaging before assuming soft-tissue sprain.
supporting_evidence: Ottawa Ankle Rules include midfoot criteria validated to catch clinically relevant fractures

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: High sensitivity in validation literature — do not invent a specific percentage here; follow local protocol.

red_flags: Bone tenderness at navicular or base of 5th MT per rules
Inability to bear weight per rules

references.citation: Stiell IG et al. Ottawa Ankle Rules. JAMA / related validation.
Bachmann LM et al. Accuracy of Ottawa ankle rules — systematic review.

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Coexistence framing — not a single-test metric.

limitations: Do not auto-blame tight calves as sole cause
recommended_examination: Map familiar pain to Achilles vs fascia tests

references.citation: Martin RL et al. Heel Pain CPG. JOSPT.
